problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. The available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 42 cubic meters, revenue $80
* Container 2: volume 12 cubic meters, revenue $69
* Container 3: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue $257
* Container 4: volume 43 cubic meters, revenue $74
* Container 5: volume 18 cubic meters, revenue $143
* Container 6: volume 9 cubic meters, revenue $30
* Container 7: volume 12 cubic meters, revenue $189
* Container 8: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue $175
* Container 9: volume 13 cubic meters, revenue $58
* Container 10: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue $263
* Container 11: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $138
* Container 12: volume 21 cubic meters, revenue $107
* Container 13: volume 41 cubic meters, revenue $69
* Container 14: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue $134
* Container 15: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue $214
* Container 16: volume 50 cubic meters, revenue $62
* Container 17: volume 18 cubic meters, revenue $208
* Container 18: volume 36 cubic meters, revenue $192
* Container 19: volume 3 cubic meters, revenue $179
* Container 20: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue $211

The vehicle has a maximum capacity of 363 cubic meters. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
